schema.title: IUIDocument
schema.description: The project-defined iui/1 wire contract. Semantic validation additionally enforces safe expressions, data and URLs. Native nodes are recognized but unsupported by the portable renderer.

contracts.text:
## 状态与表达式

`state` 保存字符串、有限数值或布尔值。引用写作 `{ "$": "gain" }`，计算写作 `{ "op": "mul", "args": [12, { "$": "gain" }] }`。

可用操作符：`add`、`sub`、`mul`、`div`、`max`、`min`、`round`、`abs`、`clamp`、`gt`、`lt`、`eq`、`if`、`format`。它们是受约束的数据树，不是 JavaScript 源码。未知引用、循环依赖、非法参数、除零及非有限结果会被拒绝。

需要直接求值时，可从主入口导入 `evaluateValue` 和 `evaluateState`；通常由控件与渲染器自动处理即可。

# API and security model

`iui/1` is data, never executable source. Content text is inserted through text nodes. The only HTML sink is KaTeX's generated visual HTML plus accessible MathML with `trust:false`, bounded expansion/size, and strict parsing; model HTML never enters that sink directly. Unsupported TeX falls back to visible source.

## Validation

The JSON Schema is generated from `scripts/generate-schema.mjs`. TypeScript declarations and the Ajv standalone validator are generated in the same step. CI rejects drift. Browser code imports the already generated validator, avoiding runtime `new Function` and allowing a script hash CSP without `unsafe-eval`.

`validateDocument(input)` returns `{ok:true,document}` or `{ok:false,issues}`. It accepts plain JSON values only; custom prototypes, accessors, cyclic objects, reserved keys, nonfinite numbers, and excessive values/text/depth are rejected before Ajv traversal. Semantics additionally reject unknown references, computed cycles, bad operator arities/types, numerical errors, duplicate IDs, unknown state bindings, broken topology endpoints, malformed table widths, invalid chart data, and unsafe resource declarations.

`evaluateValue(value,state,computed)` evaluates a constrained expression and throws on invalid input. `evaluateState(document,override)` returns validated, frozen state/computed results or issues. Controller state updates use this checked path. Numeric operators do not coerce strings. `if` is lazy at evaluation but both branches are inspected for references and types; runtime arithmetic errors still reject the state transition.

Limits include 64 JSON nesting levels, 2,000 node-like objects, 50,000 values, a two-million-UTF-16-code-unit text budget (including JSON keys, retained across merged state updates), and schema-specific row/series/child limits. These limits reduce resource exhaustion; they are not a promise of fixed latency for every valid document.

## Browser boundary

No raw HTML, CSS, JS, callback, import, network action, form submission, or arbitrary AppBlock is accepted. SVG uses a fixed shape list and numeric/color/geometry attribute allowlists. `native` is recognized solely to report `UNSUPPORTED_NATIVE`. It does not load an adapter.

Model URLs are limited to the documented link/image policy. Remote images require a reader action and use no-referrer. URLs still lead to third parties when a reader activates them; validation does not certify the destination's content or privacy. Callers handling confidential documents should avoid remote URLs altogether.

Compiled inline HTML applies a CSP containing the exact SHA-256 of its runtime. It blocks network connections, objects, forms, base URL changes, and remote scripts/fonts; font-src data: permits the bundled official WOFF2 fonts. Styles allow inline rules because the renderer writes bounded, host-owned numeric/enum properties. The host browser's CSP remains authoritative for `mount`; pass `styles:false` and serve the stylesheet when embedding under a stricter host policy.

`compileHtml(input,{assets:'inline',backend:'portable',lang})` emits one self-contained HTML file. `compileArtifact(input,{assets:'shared',assetBase:'./iui-assets/',lang})` also returns an asset map with safe relative file paths. Shared output is intended for a static HTTP server; no claim is made for every browser's file-origin shared-script policy. Both reject unsupported backends.

## Lifecycle and scope

Controllers isolate state. `update` validates the complete next document and resets state. `setState` merges a scalar patch, verifies all bindings and derived values, then updates existing nodes without replacing focused controls. `dispose` is idempotent and removes its owned elements, listeners, and resize observer. External DOM edits by the embedding host are outside this contract.

The library does not authenticate users, persist documents, store credentials, run simulations as scientific truth, fetch sources, or verify model-generated facts. Applications remain responsible for provenance, permissions, and their host threat model.

JSON Schema string `maxLength` and evaluated Value/state string maxima use Unicode code points. A Value string accepts at most 12,000 code points, including astral characters, while the independent whole-document resource budget still counts UTF-16 storage units. The resolved evaluation context (state, computed scalars and the evaluated Value) is checked against the same storage budget before DOM creation or refresh; accepted documents therefore do not defer that rejection until rendering. Native form minLength/maxLength constraints retain HTML UTF-16 semantics; they do not redefine the global string contract.

# Supplied entity cards and overviews

`entity-card` and `entity-overview` are finite, authored presentations. They do not discover entities, infer facts, resolve accounts, execute arbitrary action payloads, navigate, send telemetry or perform domain-specific medical/account work. URLs are only used for explicitly supplied images under the consent boundary below.

## Data

Both require a nonblank accessible `label`; accept optional `id`, `disabled`, `status` (`resolved` by default, `pending`, `failed`), `fallback`, and `loadImageLabel`. Pending shows an accessible loading block; failed displays `fallback` or hides the component. Active image/action/item data is rejected in unresolved states.

- `entity-card`: required resolved `title`; optional `subtitle`, `image: {src,alt?}` or null, `actionId` and `actionLabel`. Missing/null image preserves the 4:3 placeholder. Title and subtitle use bounded visual line clamping; complete text remains in the DOM.
- `entity-overview`, default `variant: single`: required `item: {id,title,images,metadata,description?,actionId?,actionLabel?,disabled?}`. Metadata records are literal `{label,value}` strings. Empty metadata and missing description omit their sections. Zero images omit the mosaic; one fills it; two share it; three or more display only the first three as one large/two small. Supplied images are capped at 12 and metadata at 20. The single card is capped at 362 CSS pixels and metadata can scroll horizontally.
- `entity-overview`, `variant: carousel`: requires `items` instead of `item`, maximum 50 with unique IDs. Reuses the existing carousel renderer. Each tile uses up to the first two supplied images, a 180-pixel mosaic and desktop width 360 pixels, with 84% narrow/mobile presentation. Optional `title` captions the collection; empty items display `emptyLabel` or “No entities”. `mobile` is a supplied layout hint, not device detection.

No arbitrary user child tree is accepted. All generated card content is passive text and layout; action and image-consent buttons are siblings, never nested controls. Metadata content is rendered as a definition list, not interpreted as HTML. Unknown action payloads and linked/nested interactive child nodes are rejected structurally.

## Actions and image permission

An `actionId` adds a native button with supplied `actionLabel` or an accessible title-derived label. Activation emits `iui:entity-action` with frozen detail `{id,entityId,actionId}`. `id` is the component ID or null; card `entityId` is its supplied ID or null, overview `entityId` is the item ID. The event bubbles, is cancelable and is not composed. There is no default remote effect or navigation, whether accepted or canceled. Passive metadata/background clicks use the same single intent.

Allowed inline raster data images load locally. HTTP(S) images initially show a separate consent button and do not assign any image source. Consent emits cancelable, non-composed, bubbling `iui:entity-image-request` with frozen `{id,entityId,src}`. Only an accepted, still-current request starts that exact image using the shared supplied-image renderer. Preventing default leaves it unloaded. This does not activate the entity action. SVG data and unsafe schemes are rejected. Failed bitmaps hide; replacement/disposal clears owned sources. No image lookup, original-resolution discovery or account request occurs.

Supplied/current disabled state, first-legend fieldset rules, hidden/inert ancestry, canceled activation, permanent ownership retirement and update/dispose are honored. A shared per-component intent gate covers event-constructor reentry. Errors remain observable. A native form reset emits neither action nor image consent; the component has no form-edited data to reset.

## Integration and verification limits

Installer: `installEntitySchema({node,defs})` in `scripts/entity-schema.mjs`; both canonical nodes belong to the base group. Semantic hook: `inspectEntity(node,path,add,isSafeURL)`. Rendering: `renderEntity(context,node,root,container)` where root/container are the same mounted owner/host supplied to the existing image/link renderers. Add `entity.css` to both embedded renderer styles and build output.

The domain-only checkpoint excludes temporary shared dispatch/style/generator/build wiring and generated schemas. Regenerate with the project generator after serial integration; a domain-only commit alone is not protocol availability. No captured resources are part of this implementation.

Tests exercise validation, finite variants, empty/null/failure, image consent cancellation, passive structure, literal metadata, local actions, disabled/fieldset gates, constructor reentry/errors, update/dispose, image late-source-setter compensation, ordinary carousel resize and repeated resource cleanup, ownership removal and compiled standalone execution. Browser suites define actual keyboard/scroll/narrow-layout checks; discovery is not native execution or pixel acceptance.

A separate adversarial probe identified an inherited shared-carousel limitation: a requestAnimationFrame registration that synchronously replaces the mount before returning its frame ID does not cancel that late ID on the older shared implementation. Ordinary update/dispose cleanup passes; this late-registration case needs a shared-carousel fix and retest before broad lifecycle acceptance. The entity domain does not duplicate or replace the shared carousel's resource machinery.

The original late requestAnimationFrame ID registration failure is retained as negative evidence. The shared47c1d8 lifecycle repair was applied in this integration; the author independently replayed the same actual mount probe and observed cancellation of the late909 ID. Original entity domain files alone did not include that repair.

## Source selection and precise validation

`entities/cards` registers these two existing types from the original installer. `ENTITY_DATA` rejects whitespace-only top-level direct strings except subtitle; subtitle retains empty/whitespace support. For every overview item it checks all direct string fields, plus every metadata label and value. Image alt strings retain their structural empty/whitespace allowance; each supplied image src passes the shared safe-image URL policy. No extra blanket trim rule is applied to image alt.

An actionLabel requires an actionId on the card or corresponding overview item. Overview item IDs must be unique within its selected collection. The structural single/carousel branches prohibit supplying both item and items; pending/failed branches prohibit item/items, while a card prohibits active image/actionId there. Any permitted fields still undergo semantic validation. The full `validateDocument` check remains required beyond the selected structural package, before mounting or compiling.
